title: How Curse Inc. chose Huntsville, Alabama over Silicon Valley to solve its hiring bottleneck
summary: Hubert Thieblot explains why Curse moved HQ from San Francisco to Huntsville. Hiring was the biggest growth constraint, and competing with well-funded Bay Area companies for talent was not a game worth playing. He walks through the five criteria used to pick a city and the logic of being a big fish in a smaller, rising market.

principles.text: As a company scales, growing the team fast enough becomes the biggest challenge, so design your location and strategy around talent.
principles.quote: As we have grown, the biggest challenge we face is to grow our team to keep up with our company.

principles.text: Don't fight much larger, better-funded rivals head-on for talent; pick a different battlefield.
principles.quote: we looked at the environment surrounding talent and decided we couldn’t just “slug it out” with the very large and very well-funded companies that exist in San Francisco

principles.text: Evaluate HQ location on explicit criteria: talent pool, work-life balance, business environment, cost efficiency, and potential.
principles.quote: The factors that were most important to us were the following;

principles.text: Look for a talent market with real depth but not so much competition that hiring becomes slow and prohibitively expensive.
principles.quote: We needed a location with a strong tech presence but not so much that competition would make securing employees prohibitively expensive or take so long that it slows down our production.

principles.text: Optimize for value per dollar, not simply the cheapest option; saving money alone isn't the goal.
principles.quote: the key isn’t to simply save. We could put a team in another country for that. Rather, we wanted to get the most bang for our buck

principles.text: Skip the trendy default and be an early, important part of a rising ecosystem rather than a drop in the bucket in a big one.
principles.quote: Curse would rather blaze a trail toward an up and coming community and be a part of its evolution from the very beginning.
